content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: outage message, chat deflection, callback, break delays on both queues and overtime for 55 payments agents. Predicted 83.2% service level for 10:45-12:45 at ₹10,275.","why":"The spike is caused by the UPI switch outage (P1 incident INC-20261006-6998, opened 10:31), not by a staffing problem. Payments calls hit 213 against 111.9 forecast (+90%), and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Service level fell to 4.7%, with 59 calls abandoned, even though staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents). R1 cuts demand with the outage message, 20% chat deflection of payment_status_enquiry and callback. It adds capacity with overtime for 55 payments agents, delayed breaks on both queues and cancelled payments coaching. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the disruption window: payments 86.6%, general 77.5%, abandon rate 3.7%, rest of day 89.2%. There are no policy violations and no escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["P3 (₹7,575) is ₹2,700 cheaper but reaches only 77.5%, just short of target, with 5.2% abandons.","R2 (₹11,355) reaches 88.0% and lifts general to 91.1%, but costs ₹1,080 more than R1 for a result already above target.","Under R1 the general queue sits at 77.5%, below 80%. Its breaks are delayed to protect it, but it is the weaker queue.","Doing nothing (P0) leaves service level at 29.4% with 22.2% abandons. The low-cost plans P1 and P2 only reach 39.5% and 49.8%.","Staffing-only (P4) costs ₹8,265 for just 52.6%. Overtime without the demand-cutting levers is poor value."],"watch":"Track the UPI incident status. If it is resolved early, release overtime and turn off the outage message. If it runs past 12:45, re-plan. Check that enough of the 55 payments agents actually accept overtime from 11:15, and watch the general queue's service level, which is forecast below target at 77.5%."}
